messages.content: I need to start comparing flights for another museum trip. I have to be in Boston by Tuesday evening, January 13, for a transfer Wednesday morning, and then I have an inspection in Providence Friday afternoon. I’ll be traveling alone from Atlanta.

I can compare this as an open-jaw itinerary: Atlanta to Boston on Tuesday, January 13, then Providence to Atlanta either Friday, January 16 or Saturday, January 17. Before I narrow it down, what time can you leave Atlanta Tuesday, and how late are you willing to arrive in Boston?
I can leave after 10:00 a.m. I need enough time to get to the hotel and be settled before 8:00 p.m., so I would rather land by 6:00.

That gives us several workable Tuesday choices. The strongest nonstop candidates are a Delta flight leaving Atlanta at 11:20 a.m. and arriving Boston at 1:58 p.m. for $214, and another leaving at 2:10 p.m. and arriving at 4:48 p.m. for $238. JetBlue has a 12:45 p.m. nonstop arriving at 3:22 p.m. for $201. Those prices are for the outbound portion in regular economy, not basic economy.
Keep the 11:20 Delta and the 12:45 JetBlue in the comparison. The later Delta leaves less margin than I want if Boston traffic is bad.
I’ll retain those two outbound options. For the return, do you know the earliest time you could reach Providence airport Friday, or is that what is still pending?
That is still pending. The inspection starts at 1:00 p.m. and may finish around 3:30, but the registrar has warned me it could run until 5:00. I do not want to assume the early finish.

Understood. Friday has one practical nonstop to Atlanta at 6:35 p.m., arriving at 9:28 p.m., currently $247 in regular economy. It would be reasonable only if you left the inspection by about 4:30, assuming the site is in central Providence and you use a car to the airport. A later one-stop itinerary leaves at 7:50 p.m., connects in Washington, and reaches Atlanta at 11:46 p.m. for $226, but even that becomes tight if the inspection runs to 5:00.
Please do not rule Friday out, but label both of those as conditional. What does Saturday look like if I stay one more night?

Saturday offers more room. There is a 9:15 a.m. Delta nonstop from Providence arriving Atlanta at 12:08 p.m. for $219, a 12:40 p.m. Delta nonstop arriving at 3:34 p.m. for $236, and an American one-stop through Charlotte leaving at 10:25 a.m. and arriving at 2:18 p.m. for $198. The American connection is 52 minutes. All three are regular economy fares.
The 9:15 Saturday flight is earlier than I need after a long week. Keep the 12:40 Delta and the 10:25 American. How do the full itinerary totals compare with each outbound?

Using the current segment prices, the Tuesday 11:20 a.m. Delta outbound combines to $461 with Friday’s 6:35 p.m. nonstop, $440 with Friday’s 7:50 p.m. connection, $450 with Saturday’s 12:40 p.m. Delta nonstop, or $412 with Saturday’s 10:25 a.m. American connection. The Tuesday 12:45 p.m. JetBlue outbound produces totals of $448, $427, $437, and $399 respectively. These totals do not include checked-bag or seat-selection charges.

The crates and paperwork will move separately, so I will only have a carry-on. I do want a standard economy ticket that can be changed if the inspection schedule moves. Are all of these fares changeable?

The Delta and JetBlue regular economy fares can be changed without a change fee, though a fare difference would apply. The American fare shown is Main Cabin and also permits changes with a fare difference. None is refundable to the original payment method. I have excluded basic economy from the comparison.
Good. Is there any issue mixing JetBlue outbound with Delta or American on the return? I am thinking about disruption handling rather than loyalty benefits.

The flights would be issued as separate one-way tickets, so mixing carriers is allowed. The tradeoff is that neither airline has responsibility for the other segment, but because the flights are on different days and in different cities, that creates little practical connection risk. A cancellation on the outbound would still need to be handled by JetBlue rather than by the return carrier.
That is acceptable. Compare the two Friday returns more closely. I suspect the nonstop is worth the difference, but I need to understand the airport timing.

The nonstop is the cleaner Friday choice. It costs $21 more than the Washington connection, arrives 2 hours 18 minutes earlier, and avoids a 58-minute evening connection. For a 6:35 p.m. departure, I would target arriving at T. F. Green by 5:15 p.m. With no checked bag, leaving central Providence around 4:35 should ordinarily provide a workable margin, but a 5:00 inspection finish would make it unsuitable. The 7:50 p.m. option supports an airport arrival around 6:30 and is more plausible after a late finish, although you would not reach Atlanta until nearly midnight.
Then keep the Friday nonstop as the first Friday choice and the connection only as a fallback. For Saturday, is the $38 savings on American worth the connection compared with Delta?

The American option leaves 2 hours 15 minutes earlier but arrives only 1 hour 16 minutes earlier because of the Charlotte connection. The Delta flight is nonstop and keeps Saturday morning less rushed. The American itinerary is financially better at $198, but the Delta return is operationally simpler and gives you more recovery time after the inspection. Both remain viable; the choice is essentially $38 versus a nonstop and later departure.
Please leave both Saturday choices open. Can you give me a concise comparison I can send to the exhibition director? Nothing should be booked or held yet.

Open-jaw trip under review for January 13-17: fly Atlanta to Boston Tuesday for the Wednesday transfer, travel separately from Boston to Providence, and return after Friday’s inspection. Outbound choices are Delta nonstop at 11:20 a.m.-1:58 p.m. for $214 or JetBlue nonstop at 12:45-3:22 p.m. for $201. If the inspection ends early enough Friday, the preferred return is Delta nonstop at 6:35-9:28 p.m.; full airfare would be $461 with the Delta outbound or $448 with JetBlue. A 7:50 p.m. one-stop return reaching Atlanta at 11:46 p.m. remains a late-finish fallback, totaling $440 or $427. If Saturday is required, the choices are American at 10:25 a.m.-2:18 p.m. via Charlotte, totaling $412 or $399, and Delta nonstop at 12:40-3:34 p.m., totaling $450 or $437. All quoted options are changeable regular economy with fare differences applicable, and no flight has been booked or held. The unresolved decision is whether Friday’s inspection will end in time for an evening departure.

A new solo museum trip is being compared for January 13-17: Atlanta to Boston Tuesday ahead of a Wednesday exhibition transfer, followed by a Friday afternoon receiving inspection in Providence. Two Tuesday nonstop outbound choices and both Friday and Saturday return structures remain open. Friday departure depends on when the inspection ends; nothing has been booked or held.
